---
title: "Add-On Packages"
---

## Why Packages?

You've now learned how to use dozens of R's built-in functions, such as `mean()`, `round()`, `sqrt()`, `sum()`, and many
more. These all ship with R itself, ready to use the moment you open RStudio. But R's built-in functions can't cover
every possible task. For almost any specialized analysis, fitting a particular kind of statistical model, reading a
particular file format, making a particular kind of plot, someone in the R community has almost certainly already
written and shared the code to do it.

## What Is a Package?

A **package** is simply a collection of functions (plus, sometimes, data and documentation) that someone else has
written and bundled up for others to use — the exact same idea as the individual functions you've already been
calling, just packaged together in a reusable, installable unit. Just like you don't need to know how `mean()` is
implemented internally to use it, you don't need to know how a package's functions work internally to use them either.

The following list shows a few common data-analysis tasks and some packages that provide relevant functions for each.

- Treating missing data using multiple imputation
  - [mice](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mice/index.html)
  - [Amelia](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/Amelia/index.html)
  - [mi](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mi/index.html)
- Structural equation modeling
  - [lavaan](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lavaan/index.html)
  - [OpenMx](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/OpenMx/index.html)
- Multilevel regression modeling
  - [lme4](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lme4/index.html)
  - [nlme](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nlme/index.html)
- For all but the most trivial data processing, manipulation, and visualization, the [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/)
packages are virtually obligatory.

Over the rest of this tutorial, you'll learn the two steps every package requires before you can use it: **installing**
it (once) and **loading** it (every time you start a new R session and want to use it).
